headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection via shared document content and MCP/browser surfaces; data leakage and cascading errors are moderate, with compliance risk low.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU can use an MCP server and ingests local PDFs/DOCX/XLSX; PaddleOCR can run browsers and process documents/images. A shared workspace or copy-paste bridge is not documented, so direct hijack is unproven, but document content from A could be treated as instructions by B if bridged. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange document text through a shared file, clipboard, or MCP channel
IF B parses A's extracted text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable any shared clipboard or shared folder between the agents
Route A's outputs through a plain-text sanitizer before B reads them
Require B to treat all A output as untrusted data
Add a manual review step for any instruction-like text
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to A outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU touches PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, JSON, tables, formulas, and OCR text; PaddleOCR touches documents and images. Neither profile shows secrets handling or a shared filesystem, but if they operate on the same workspace, sensitive document contents can flow from A into B's processing. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default document workflows, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or document set
IF either agent uploads document contents to a remote inference backend
mitigations: Separate input directories for each agent
Remove sensitive files before handing A output to B
Use local-only execution for both agents
Check logs for document-content uploads
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MinerU has no filesystem write, git, or shell execution, while PaddleOCR only shows browser and API use. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The only overlap is document processing and allowlisted egress, so contention is limited unless an external orchestrator grants shared mutable resources not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same mutable resource
IF both agents are asked to modify the same document artifact concurrently
mitigations: Assign separate output paths
Serialize edits to shared artifacts
Keep one agent read-only
Use file locks in the orchestrator
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted text, tables, and OCR output that PaddleOCR could consume as downstream input. No verification or provenance controls are shown, so B may treat A's extraction as authoritative. Because both are document-processing agents, a bad extraction can cascade into incorrect OCR/translation or structured outputs, but no direct action-taking authority is documented.
conditions: IF B consumes A's extracted text or tables without independent verification
IF A's OCR or layout errors are forwarded into B's final output
mitigations: Insert a validation step between A and B
Compare B output against the original source document
Flag low-confidence extractions for review
Keep provenance metadata with each field
requires-engineering: add confidence-based gating

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source document-processing tools with no declared secrets handling, certifications, or residency constraints. The only compliance concern visible is generic document handling, and no specific mismatch is documented. Because the profiles do not show PHI, EU-only, or retention differences, this is a low-confidence, low-severity compliance gap.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is processed through either agent
IF the deployment imposes retention or residency rules not reflected in the profiles
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in this pair
Document retention settings
Confirm deployment region
Review logs for sensitive fields
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
